chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Baṣīr, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:
“ʿAlī عليه السلام used to administer eighty lashes for wine and nabīdh, upon the free man, the slave, the Jew, and the Christian.”
I said: “What is the case of the Jew and the Christian?”
He said: “They are not permitted to make their drinking public; that is to be in their houses.”

key_terms.النَّبِيذِ: nabīdh, an intoxicating drink mentioned alongside wine
key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيَّ: the Christian, mentioned regarding public display of drinking
key_terms.الْحُرَّ: the free person, as opposed to a slave
key_terms.الْخَمْرِ: wine or intoxicating drink subject to legal punishment
key_terms.الْيَهُودِيَّ: the Jew, mentioned regarding public display of drinking
key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ: eighty, the number of lashes prescribed here
key_terms.يُظْهِرُوا: to make public or display openly

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about the hadd for drinking wine and its application to Jews and Christians?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal punishment for drinking intoxicants and indicates that it was applied broadly, including to free persons, slaves, Jews, and Christians. It also clarifies that non-Muslims under Muslim rule are not to display drinking publicly, but may do so privately in their homes.
